NONE: A1 large in size or amount
（尺寸或數量）大的，巨大的
A2 informal older or more like an adult
年齡較大的；長大的

before noun: C2 [ before noun ] informal used to add emphasis

NONE: A2 important, because of being powerful, or having a lot of influence or a serious effect
重要的；影響大的；嚴重的
› to be important or famous in a particular place or type of work
重要；名氣大
C1 informal If a product or activity is big, it is extremely popular.
流行的，受歡迎的

example: He's a big man.
他是個身材高大的人。
Could I try these shoes in a bigger size?
這雙鞋我能試一雙大一點的嗎？
They have a big house in the country.
他們在鄉下有一幢大房子。
She has blonde hair and big blue eyes.
她有一頭金黃的頭髮和一雙大大的藍眼睛。
She had a big pay rise.
她的薪水增加了很多。
I had a great big slice of chocolate cake for dessert.
我吃了一大塊巧克力蛋糕作為甜點。
A thousand people took part in the region's biggest ever cycle race.
有1000人參加了本地區有史以來規模最大的自行車賽。
informal She's always been a big spender (= she has always spent a lot of money).
她總是揮霍金錢。
informal You're not a very big eater, are you? (= You do not eat a lot.)
你吃得並不多，對嗎？
Her big (= older) sister/brother told her to go away.
她姐姐／哥哥叫她走開。
I'm ashamed of you. You're big enough to know better (= at an age where you should know that your behaviour is not acceptable).
我為你感到羞恥。你這麼大了，該知道好歹了。
You're a big bully!
你真是一個大惡霸！
He fell for her in a big way (= was greatly attracted to her).
他被她深深吸引了。
He had a big decision to make.
他要做一個重要的決定。
There's a big difference between starting up a business and just talking about it.
真正創辦一間企業和只是口頭說說，是有很大區別的。
The big story in the news this week is the mayor's resignation.
本週的重要新聞是市長的請辭。
The four biggest banks are all planning to cut their service charges.
四大銀行都在計劃降低服務收費。
They're big in Japan, but no one's heard of them here.
他們在日本的名氣很大，但這裡的人並沒有聽說過他們。
Hip-hop is still big today.
嘻哈音樂現在仍然流行。

NONE: › a large group of musicians who play jazz and dance music
（尤指過去演奏爵士樂和舞曲的）大樂隊
› a large wild animal
大型野生動物
› UK a large and powerful organization, or a powerful person
巨頭；大企業

example: Prehistoric fires may have killed off the big beasts that once roamed Australia.
史前階段的數場大火可能使一度生活在澳大利亞的大型野生動物通通滅絕。
They are the big beasts among TV networks.
他們是電視公司中的巨頭。

NONE: › a way of referring to a government, ruler, or person in authority that has complete power and tries to control people's behaviour and thoughts and limit their freedom
「大佬」；專制政府；獨裁者
big money
› powerful and influential businesses and financial organizations (= ones with a lot of influence) when considered as a group
大企業；大財團
› something that makes a lot of money
利潤高的行業，賺錢的行業

example: The party receives most of its financial support from big business.
這個政黨主要從大財團那裡獲得財力支持。
Health clubs are big business these days.
如今健身俱樂部是很賺錢的。

NONE: › a lion, tiger, or other large wild animal from the cat family
大型貓科動物

example: Tigers are among the rarest of the big cats.
老虎是稀有的大型貓科動物。

NONE: › very large sets of data that are produced by people using the internet, and that can only be stored, understood, and used with the help of special tools and methods
大數據，海量資料，大資料
› said when you do not think that what someone has said or done is important or special
沒甚麼了不起！

example: "I ran five miles this morning." "Big deal! I ran ten."
「今天早上我跑了五英里。」「沒甚麼了不起！我跑了十英里。」

NONE: › a small railway in an amusement park that travels very quickly along a narrow track that slopes and bends suddenly
（遊樂場的）雲霄飛車
› a group of seven bright stars that can only be seen in the northern part of the world
北斗七星
› informal a person who has an important or powerful position in a group or organization
大人物，要人

example: She's a big gun in city politics.
她是市政要人。
He's a big shot in advertising.
他是廣告界的大人物。

NONE: › large wild animals that are hunted and shot for sport
大獵物
› hair that forms a large shape all around the head
蓬鬆的波浪髮型

example: At that time big hair was fashionable.
那時蓬鬆的波浪髮式是很時尚的。

NONE: › an important and influential person or thing (= one with a lot of influence), especially of their particular type
（尤指某類）要人，重要的事情

example: The big hitters in the cast include Michael Caine and Ewan McGregor.
演員陣容中的大牌人物有米高‧凱恩和尤安‧麥格雷戈。

NONE: › US big leagues the top level of a particular sport, business, or activity in which there is the greatest competition and the greatest opportunity for success
（某運動、行業或活動的）頂級水準
› in the US, a group of professional sports teams that compete at the highest level, especially in baseball
（尤指美國棒球）大聯賽

example: He is about to join the big league of Formula One in time for the new season.
他即將晉身世界一級方程式拉力賽，並將參加新賽季的比賽。
For the magazine to be successful, it will have to compete in the big league against leading weekly women's magazines.
想成功的話，該雜誌就必須在主流市場和頂尖的女性週刊競爭。

NONE: › a large amount of money
大筆的錢

example: Tournament organizers need to offer big money to attract the top players.
錦標賽籌辦者需要提供大筆獎金，才能吸引高水準的運動員。

NONE: › If someone is or has a big mouth, they often say things that are meant to be kept secret.
多嘴的人

example: He is/has such a big mouth.
他太多嘴了。
He went and opened his big mouth and told them the whole story.
他去了，並且多嘴多舌地把整件事告訴了他們。
I'm sorry. I wasn't supposed to tell you! Me and my big mouth!
對不起，我不該告訴你們的。我真多嘴！

NONE: › a famous or important person
名人；重要人物

example: Are there any big names in the movie?
這齣電影裡有大明星嗎？
She's a big name in politics.
她是一位政界要人。

NONE: › to talk a lot about how excellent someone or something is, sometimes praising him, her, or it more than is deserved
（過分）誇獎，讚揚
› If you do something big time, you do it to a great degree.
很大程度上，非常
› the state of being famous or successful
出名，成功

example: "How was the interview?" "Terrible, I messed up big time."
「面試怎麼樣？」「糟透了，我完全弄砸了。」
Chrissy's into skiing big time (= likes skiing a lot).
克麗茜很喜歡滑雪。
She finally hit the big time (= became famous or successful) with her latest novel.
她最終因為新出版的小說而一舉成名。
You've really made the big time now (= become famous or successful).
你現在真是功成名就了。

NONE: › the largest toe on your foot
大腳趾
› the main tent in a circus
（馬戲團的）大帳篷
› a large, vertical wheel in an amusement park with seats that stay horizontal as the wheel turns round
（遊樂場的）摩天輪
› a long, difficult word, or a word that expresses a serious or important idea
又長又艱深的詞彙；表達嚴肅或重要概念的字眼

example: He tried to impress his teachers by using big words in all his essays.
他在所有的作文中，試圖以又長又艱深的詞彙以給老師留下好印象。

NONE: › a very large shop that sells a large number of products, usually at low prices
倉儲式商場，超級市場

example: The rise of chain retailers led to the supremacy of big-box stores like Kmart, Target, and Wal-Mart.
連鎖零售商店的崛起造就了諸如凱馬特、塔吉特和沃爾瑪等超級市場的霸主地位。

NONE: › kind and generous
善良的，慷慨的
› Big-ticket things are things that are expensive to buy, such as cars or furniture.
昂貴的
› the crime of marrying a person while already legally married to someone else
重婚罪

example: In court, he admitted that he had committed bigamy.
在法庭上，他承認犯了重婚罪。
Compare
monogamy

NONE: › a large creature like a human covered in hair that some people believe exists in the northwest of the US and western Canada
（據說曾生活在美國西北部和加拿大西部的）北美野人
› something that is very important or successful
重要的事情；成功的事情

example: His new movie will be the Hollywood biggie this summer.
他的新電影將是今夏好萊塢的重頭戲。

NONE: › someone who thinks that they are more important or cleverer than they really are
自命不凡的人

example: He's always boasting. He's such a bighead!
他老是吹牛。真是個自負的傢夥！

NONE: › thinking that you are more important or more intelligent than you really are
自負的，傲慢的

example: She's so bigheaded!
她自負得不得了！
Compare
swollen head

NONE: › behaviour that shows that you think you are important or intelligent
自負的行為

example: Answering questions in class was seen as a sign of big-headedness.
在課堂上回答問題被看作是自負的標誌。

NONE: › a person who has strong, unreasonable beliefs and who does not like other people who have different beliefs or a different way of life
偏執的人，固執己見的人

example: a religious bigot
宗教偏執狂
He was known to be a loud-mouthed, opinionated bigot.
大家都知道他是一個高談闊論、固執己見的偏執狂。

NONE: › a person who has an important or powerful position
大人物，要人

example: We were invited to a lunch with local bigwigs.
我們受邀與當地要人共進午餐。
